title: Kali-GPT MCP tool parameters permit shell command injection
summary: Unsanitized scanner parameters reach shell=True in the MCP server. An MCP client or prompt-injected agent can execute commands as the server user.

severity.rationale: An attacker must control tool arguments or influence agent calls. This common agent boundary can expose the MCP server process to arbitrary command execution.

affected.note: The CVE record identifies affected code through commit a608c74 and specifies no fixed release.

exposure: Exposed deployments accept untrusted tool parameters, directly or through prompt-injected agent calls.

params.instructions: Identify the Kali-GPT checkout revision and check for the command-injection behavior described by CVE-2026-117569; version numbers alone are insufficient.

remediation.action: Contain exposure and apply a verified fix
remediation.details: As a containment recommendation, disconnect the vulnerable server from untrusted workflows until a vendor-verified patch is deployed. The cited record provides no fixed release.
remediation.risk: Medium. Disabling the affected capability interrupts dependent workflows.

verification: Confirm the version or revision and review the affected configuration before restoring untrusted input.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review.
